info.title: organox
info.description:
Business administration for a small or medium enterprise (stock and supplies). Single-tenant.

**Authentication**: except `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, every route requires the `session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict). Without it, routes return `401`.

**Errors**: all error responses use `application/problem+json` (RFC 7807). A `429` also includes the `Retry-After` header in seconds.

**Decimals**: always transmitted as **strings** (`"1500.50"`, `"12.5"`), never numbers, to avoid losing precision.

post.description:
Returns the `session` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict) and the user.

`429` means the account is locked after failed attempts; includes
`Retry-After` with the remaining seconds.

post.summary: End the session on the server, not just the client.

get.summary: Authenticated user in the current request.

post.description:
Requires the current password. The new one must satisfy the password rule.
Every other session of the user is revoked; the session making the change
remains valid.

401.description: Wrong current password or no session

get.summary: List payment methods with the wallet each one pays into.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description:
Include deactivated rows. The settings screen needs them so a wallet can
be brought back; the POS does not.

post.summary: Create a payment method pointing at a wallet.
post.description:
This is the endpoint that makes a new method a data change instead of a
deploy.

patch.summary: Rename, re-point or (de)activate a payment method.
patch.description:
Re-pointing changes where future money lands. Movements already recorded keep
the wallet they hit: the ledger is history, not a live join.

404.description: Payment method or wallet not found

get.summary: List the catalog with calculated stock.

post.description: A service does not track stock: `min_stock` is rejected with 422.

get.summary: Product details, including calculated current stock.
get.description: `stock` is `null` for services: not applicable, not zero.

post.summary:
Soft deletion. Idempotent. Never deletes: a product with movements retains
its history.

post.description:
`quantity` is always positive; `reason` determines the sign. An outflow
that would leave stock negative is rejected with 409.

422.description: Invalid input or service without stock

post.summary: Open a sale draft, or return the one already open.
post.description:
A user has **one** draft at a time: reloading the sale screen does not
create new carts.

get.summary: Sale with its items and server-calculated total.

post.summary: Cancel a draft. Does not touch the stock ledger, because it never did.

post.description:
In one transaction: validate stock with the product row locked, check that
the payments add up to the total, write an outflow movement per item and a
money movement per payment, then close the sale. Any rejection leaves **no**
movements and no status change.

409.description: Insufficient stock or sale already closed

422.description: Sale empty, payments missing, wrong sum or unusable method

get.summary:
The credits of a sale: what was charged, what came back and where the money
of each note went. A draft has no stored total, so the charged lines decide
it; the refunded total is the sum of the notes already issued.

post.summary: Return part or all of a charged sale.
post.description:
Creates a credit note: the goods rejoin stock and the money leaves the
wallets that received the payment, in proportion to it. The sale is never
edited; a sale can be returned in several notes, and the total returned per
product can never exceed what was sold.

409.description: Sale not completed, or more than what can still be returned

post.summary: Add a product to the draft. If already present, add the quantity.
post.description: Returns the recalculated sale: the client does not add anything.

422.description: Invalid quantity or item is a service

put.summary: Set an item's quantity. Quantity 0 removes it.

delete.summary: Remove an item from the draft.

get.summary: List every user, ordered by email. Only `owner`.

403.description: Role does not permit managing users
Role does not permit managing users

put.description:
No current password is requested: the owner cannot know it. Every session
of the target is revoked, except the caller's when resetting their own.

403.description: Role does not permit managing users

get.summary: List wallets with their calculated balance.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description:
Include deactivated rows. The settings screen needs them so a wallet can
be brought back; the POS does not.

post.summary: Create a wallet (a cash box, a bank account).

get.summary: One wallet with its calculated balance.

patch.summary: Rename or (de)activate a wallet. Wallets are never deleted.

get.summary: Movements of one wallet, newest first.

post.summary: Record money leaving or entering a wallet by hand.
post.description:
`sale_payment` is rejected with 422: a collection enters the ledger only by
charging a sale.

CompleteSaleRequest.description:
How the sale is paid. Required: a sale never closes without saying where the
money went.

payment_movement_ids.description:
One movement per payment, so the client can follow the money into its
wallets without a second request.

CreateCreditNoteRequest.description: A return. The total is not sent: the server calculates it.

reason.description: Why the goods came back. Required, and kept on the document.

price.description:
Documented as `string` although the server also accepts numbers:
`rust_decimal` deserializes both, but the frontend contract—and the only
one preserving precision—is the string. See `docs/api-contract.md`.

CreditNoteLineRequest.description: One line to return. The price is not sent: it is the one charged on the sale.

sale_id.description: The sale being corrected. The sale itself never changes.

total.description: Calculated by the server from the returned quantities.

CreditableLineResponse.description:
A charged line, with the quantity already credited and what can still come
back.

reused.description: `true` if the existing open draft was reused.

kind.description:
`expense`, `adjustment_in` or `adjustment_out`. `sale_payment` is
rejected: that money is recorded by charging a sale.

signed_quantity.description:
Signed quantity: what the client needs to show the stock effect without
replicating the sign rule.

wallet_id.description:
The wallet this method pays into. The UI shows its name so nobody
charges into the wrong account without noticing.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 error body. Same shape for every status code.

status.description: HTTP status, repeated in the body for clients that do not read headers.

title.description: Human-readable, stable summary of the problem.

type.description: URI identifying the problem type. Currently always `about:blank`.

ProductKind.description: A catalog item may or may not track stock.

limit.description: Page size actually applied (the request defaults to 50, is capped at 200).

offset.description: Offset of `items[0]` in the filtered set.

total.description:
How many products the filters match in total, ignoring the page. A client
needs this to tell a full page from the last one.

low_stock.description: `null` when not applicable (service) or no threshold is configured.

price.description:
String, not number: a JSON `float` loses precision for money and
fractional quantities. The client parses it as a decimal.

stock.description: `null` for services: not zero, but "not applicable".

SaleCreditNotesResponse.description: The sale's credits: its charged lines and the notes already issued.

quantity.description:
Quantity as a string: `numeric(12,3)` does not fit in a float without
losing precision for fractional quantities.

SalePaymentRequest.description: One payment of the charge. A sale can be paid with several.

amount.description:
Positive. The sum of every payment must equal the total the server
calculated, or the charge is rejected with 422.

total.description: Calculated on the server. The client displays it, not decides it.

wallet_id.description:
Moving a method to another wallet changes where **future** money lands.
Nothing already recorded moves: every movement keeps the wallet it hit.

WalletMovementKind.description:
Why money moved.

This is an enum while payment methods are rows, and the asymmetry is the
point: a new method is business data the operator creates, but a new kind
always arrives with a writer, a validation and a screen — that is, with code.

amount.description: Always positive; the kind carries the sign.

payment_method_id.description: Set only for a `sale_payment`: which method was used.

sale_id.description: Set only for a `sale_payment`: which sale put this money here.

signed_amount.description:
The wallet's effect of this movement, so the client does not replicate
the sign rule.

balance.description:
Calculated: the signed sum of the wallet's movements, as a string with
two decimals. `"-1500.00"` is a valid answer — expenses can exceed what
the wallet holds.
